payload.summary: ledger-inbox.mjs add silently ignores --dry-run and writes a real queue entry
payload.context: Running `node scripts/ledger-inbox.mjs add --pri P2 --type task --summary "test" --dry-run` exits 0 and prints "Queued add request at docs/outstanding-issues-inbox/<uuid>.json". It writes the file. The flag is accepted without complaint and has no effect on this subcommand, so an operator probing the CLI's contract — the documented way to learn it, since `add` with no arguments only prints which fields are missing — creates a real request containing whatever placeholder text they used. This entry occupies the file that probe created, because the protection hook refuses to delete it.
payload.next: Either honour --dry-run on `add` (print the payload, write nothing) or reject the flag as unknown so it fails loudly. A silently-ignored flag is worse than an unsupported one: it reports success for work it did not do. Check whether `done`, `update`, `queue` and `cancel` accept it the same way.
